cp.open: Open the site in this style
cp.rounds_s: What changed each time, and why.
cp.r1_d: UI Hub styles were clustered and editorial × motion was picked. It shipped, but the look came first and the components second.
cp.r2_d: More effects were added to make it feel richer. The user called it ugly: too many accents, decoration without a job.
cp.r3_d: New rules: neutral plus one accent, and every module ported from a UI Hub component’s source code. Three home pages were built side by side.
cp.r4_d: The user kept all three. A became the default; B and C became themes. Every page was rebuilt in 10 languages and the daily update kept running.
cp.r5_d: Each change is checked at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in every style; then Lighthouse runs on the home page and a detail page. Fix, repeat.
cp.map_s: Every module on every page names the UI Hub item it was ported from. Shared rows are re-skinned by tokens.
cp.m1: Write the brief and the looks you will not use before opening any library.
cp.m2: Pick one neutral scale and one accent; keep text contrast at 4.5:1 or better.
cp.m3: For each module, choose a specific UI Hub item and port it from its source code.
cp.m4: Record the mapping: module, Hub id, preview, and any deviation with its reason.
cp.m5: Theme with tokens and fonts only, so styles switch without a reload.
cp.m6: Screenshot desktop and mobile in light and dark, run Lighthouse, fix, repeat.
